Class VenturiFlowMeter

java.lang.Object
neqsim.util.NamedBaseClass
neqsim.process.measurementdevice.MeasurementDeviceBaseClass
neqsim.process.measurementdevice.StreamMeasurementDeviceBaseClass
neqsim.process.measurementdevice.DifferentialPressureFlowMeter
neqsim.process.measurementdevice.VenturiFlowMeter
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, TransientStateParticipant<DifferentialPressureFlowMeter.DifferentialPressureFlowMeterState>, MeasurementDeviceInterface, ProcessElementInterface, NamedInterface
public class VenturiFlowMeter extends DifferentialPressureFlowMeter
Classical Venturi tube differential-pressure flow meter following ISO 5167-1 and ISO 5167-4.

The device reads the flowing density and the isentropic exponent from the connected stream, combines them with the measured differential pressure and the Venturi geometry, and reports the mass flow, the actual volume flow and the standard volume flow during a process run.

The mass flow rate is calculated from the ISO 5167-1 general equation 

 qm = C / sqrt(1 - beta ^ 4) * epsilon * (pi / 4) * d ^ 2 * sqrt(2 * dP * rho1)

where the expansibility factor epsilon is the ISO 5167-4 Venturi expression 

 epsilon = sqrt(kappa * tau ^ (2 / kappa) / (kappa - 1) * (1 - beta ^ 4) / (1 - beta ^ 4 * tau ^ (2 / kappa))
     * (1 - tau ^ ((kappa - 1) / kappa)) / (1 - tau))

with tau = p2 / p1. Note that this is the Venturi expansibility, not the ISO 5167-2 orifice approximation epsilon = 1 - (0.41 + 0.35 beta^4) dP / (kappa p1), which must not be used for Venturi tubes.

The upstream static pressure p1 is taken from the connected stream and p2 = p1 - dP. The differential pressure is either set explicitly with DifferentialPressureFlowMeter.setDifferentialPressure(double, String) (typical when a measured field value is pushed in each time step) or read from a linked DifferentialPressureTransmitter, which takes precedence when present.

Typical discharge coefficients from ISO 5167-4 for a classical Venturi tube are 0.995 (machined convergent section), 0.984 (as-cast convergent section) and 0.985 (rough-welded sheet-iron convergent section). The ISO 5167-4 expansibility is defined for p2 / p1 >= 0.75; values outside that window are still evaluated but reported by isWithinIso5167ValidityRange() as out of range.

Wet-gas operation (ISO/TR 11583)

When liquid is present the meter over-reads. Selecting VenturiFlowMeter.WetGasCorrelation.ISO_TR_11583 switches the device to the ISO/TR 11583 wet-gas Venturi method, in which the gas mass flow rate becomes 

 qm,gas = C / sqrt(1 - beta ^ 4) * epsilon * (pi / 4) * d ^ 2 * sqrt(2 * dP * rho1,gas) / Phi

with the Lockhart-Martinelli parameter X = (qm,liquid / qm,gas) sqrt(rho1,gas / rho,liquid), the gas densiometric Froude number Fr,gas, the throat Froude number Fr,gas,th = Fr,gas / beta^2.5, and 

 C     = 1 - 0.0463 exp(-0.05 Fr,gas,th) min(1, sqrt(X / 0.016))
 Phi   = sqrt(1 + CCh X + X ^ 2)
 CCh   = (rho,liquid / rho1,gas) ^ n + (rho1,gas / rho,liquid) ^ n
 n     = max(0.583 - 0.18 beta ^ 2 - 0.578 exp(-0.8 Fr,gas / H), 0.392 - 0.18 beta ^ 2)

Note that ISO/TR 11583 replaces the discharge coefficient. In wet-gas mode the value set with setDischargeCoefficient(double) is not used; the wet-gas C above is used instead, and it tends to 1 rather than to the dry-gas 0.985. Switching the correlation on therefore changes both C and adds Phi.

Since X, Fr,gas and C all depend on the gas mass flow rate, the solution is iterative, starting from C = 1 and Phi = 1 exactly as in ISO/TR 11583 Annex A.

The liquid load is supplied either as an absolute rate (setLiquidMassFlowRate(double, String)), as a liquid-to-gas mass ratio (setLiquidToGasMassRatio(double)), or taken from the phase split of the connected stream (setLiquidFromStream(boolean)). When the liquid rate is unknown, ISO/TR 11583 6.4.5 allows X to be derived from the permanent pressure loss measured at a third tapping downstream of the divergent section; see setPressureLoss(double, String). That third tapping is rarely fitted in practice.

Limitations of ISO/TR 11583. The Technical Report states that it applies to wet gas at roughly 95 % gas volume fraction or more, only to flows with a single liquid, and that it "is not intended for the oil and gas industry". Combining an aqueous and a hydrocarbon liquid phase into one effective liquid, as this class does when reading the liquid from the stream, is therefore an extension beyond the Technical Report. The correlations were derived for nitrogen, argon, natural gas and steam with water, Exxsol D80, white spirit and decane, for horizontally installed meters with a single pair of tappings. Validity is reported by isWithinIso11583ValidityRange() and getValidityViolations() rather than enforced.

Wet-gas operation (de Leeuw, 1997)

Selecting VenturiFlowMeter.WetGasCorrelation.DE_LEEUW switches to the de Leeuw (1997) correlation, reported by R.N. Steven, "Wet gas metering with a horizontally mounted Venturi meter", Flow Measurement and Instrumentation 12 (2002) 361-372, Eqs. (12)-(14). It uses the same Chisholm-form over-reading equation as ISO/TR 11583, 

 qm,gas = C / sqrt(1 - beta ^ 4) * epsilon * (pi / 4) * d ^ 2 * sqrt(2 * dP * rho1,gas) / Phi
 Phi    = sqrt(1 + CCh X + X ^ 2)
 CCh    = (rho,liquid / rho1,gas) ^ n + (rho1,gas / rho,liquid) ^ n

but with a different, purely empirical exponent that depends only on the gas densiometric Froude number and has no diameter-ratio term, 

 n = 0.41                             for Fr,gas <= 1.5
 n = 0.606 (1 - exp(-0.746 Fr,gas))    for Fr,gas >= 1.5

de Leeuw never replaces the discharge coefficient. Unlike ISO/TR 11583 Equation (4), C above is always the configured discharge coefficient; setUseWetGasDischargeCoefficient(boolean) has no effect on this correlation. This makes de Leeuw compatible with an in-service-calibrated discharge coefficient without any extra configuration.

Limitations of de Leeuw (1997). Steven (2002) independently benchmarked de Leeuw against five general two-phase Orifice Plate correlations and one other Venturi correlation on NEL wet-gas-loop data (20-60 bara, nitrogen/kerosene, 6 in ISA Controls Venturi, beta = 0.55) and found it the best performer (root-mean-square fractional deviation 0.0211, versus 0.0710 for Chisholm and 0.1260 for Smith & Leang). However, de Leeuw's own data was taken on a 4 in Venturi with beta = 0.401 and the exponent n carries no beta term, so applying it to a meter with a different diameter ratio is an extrapolation; this is reported by isWithinDeLeeuwValidityRange() and getValidityViolations() rather than enforced. The correlation also has no published Lockhart-Martinelli (X) range of its own (unlike ISO/TR 11583's 0 to 0.3) and, unlike ISO/TR 11583 6.4.5, no permanent-pressure-loss route to estimate X when the liquid rate is unknown.

    • setUseWetGasDischargeCoefficient

      public void setUseWetGasDischargeCoefficient(boolean useWetGasDischargeCoefficient)
      Controls whether the ISO/TR 11583 Equation (4) discharge coefficient replaces the configured one.

      ISO/TR 11583 pairs its own wet-gas discharge coefficient with the over-reading factor, and that is the default. However, a meter whose discharge coefficient has been calibrated in service carries meter-specific bias in that number; replacing it with the generic wet-gas value discards the calibration. Setting this to false keeps the configured discharge coefficient and applies only the over-reading factor, which departs from the Technical Report but preserves an existing calibration.

      This setting only affects VenturiFlowMeter.WetGasCorrelation.ISO_TR_11583. The de Leeuw (1997) correlation (VenturiFlowMeter.WetGasCorrelation.DE_LEEUW) never replaces the discharge coefficient, so it is unaffected either way.

      Parameters:
      useWetGasDischargeCoefficient - true to use ISO/TR 11583 Equation (4), false to keep the configured value

      Returns:

    • getEffectiveDischargeCoefficient

      public double getEffectiveDischargeCoefficient()
      Returns the discharge coefficient actually used. In dry-gas mode this is the configured value. In ISO/TR 11583 wet-gas mode it is the Equation (4) value, which replaces the configured one (unless setUseWetGasDischargeCoefficient(boolean) is false). de Leeuw (1997) never replaces the discharge coefficient, so this is always the configured value in VenturiFlowMeter.WetGasCorrelation.DE_LEEUW mode.
      Returns:

    • getRelativeUncertaintyOfCOverPhi

      public double getRelativeUncertaintyOfCOverPhi()
      Returns the relative uncertainty of C/Phi from ISO/TR 11583 6.5, Table 2. This is normally the dominant term in the gas mass flow uncertainty. Steven (2002) does not report an uncertainty band for the de Leeuw (1997) correlation, so this returns NaN in VenturiFlowMeter.WetGasCorrelation.DE_LEEUW mode rather than fabricate one.
      Returns:
      relative uncertainty as a fraction, or NaN outside ISO/TR 11583 wet-gas mode

    • solveWetGas

      private VenturiFlowMeter.WetGasResult solveWetGas()
      Returns the wet-gas evaluation for the current operating point, reusing the last solve when nothing that buildWetGasSignature() tracks has changed. Every wet-gas getter and getMassFlowRatePerSecond() go through this method, so multiple reads within the same timestep see one consistent, cheaply-repeated result instead of re-running the iterative solve on every call.
      Returns:
      the wet-gas evaluation outcome

    • buildWetGasSignature

      private double[] buildWetGasSignature()
      Builds a cheap fingerprint of every input computeWetGas() depends on (stream properties and wet-gas configuration), used by solveWetGas() to detect whether a fresh solve is required. Unset optional inputs (e.g. pressureLoss) are NaN; Arrays.equals(double[], double[]) treats NaN as equal to NaN (per its Javadoc contract), so that does not defeat the cache.
      Returns:
      fingerprint array, compared with Arrays.equals(double[], double[])

    • calcDeLeeuwExponent

      private double calcDeLeeuwExponent(double froude)
      Calculates the de Leeuw (1997) exponent n from the gas densiometric Froude number (Steven, 2002, Eqs. (13a)-(13b)). Unlike calcChisholmExponent(double, double) this has no diameter-ratio term. Below the 0.5 lower bound of the correlation the 0.41 plateau is extrapolated rather than returning NaN, so the meter never throws; the point is reported by getValidityViolations() instead.
      Parameters:
      froude - gas densiometric Froude number [-]
      Returns:
      exponent n [-]
